interactive.record:
On 21 December 2023, the Security Council unanimously adopted Resolution 2719 at meeting S/PV.9518 on financing for African Union-led peace support operations. The Council agreed to consider requests from the African Union Peace and Security Council case by case. Authorized operations would remain under African Union command and control. For operations authorized by the Council, UN assessed contributions may cover up to 75 percent of the annual operation budget. The UN and African Union are to jointly mobilize the remainder as extrabudgetary resources. The Council committed to consider viable options if significant shortfalls arise.

The US submitted amendment S/2023/1023. The amendment passed by nine votes to none, with six abstentions, before unanimous adoption of the final resolution. France abstained on the amendment and voted for the amended resolution. The United States sought an explicit ceiling to remove ambiguity and help enable timely deployment. France withheld support for the amendment because it did not clarify how funding outside assessed contributions would be made predictable. France reaffirmed support for assessed UN funding for AU-led operations. France was prepared to discuss different contribution levels from the UN and the EU. The amendment passed despite France's concern about the remainder, distinct from the US demand for an explicit ceiling.
